title: Gesture-first compactization for cost cards and sparkline charts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and prototype a gesture-first responsive pattern that compacts cost insight cards and embedded sparklines for constrained viewports and touch devices. The goal is to preserve readability of top-line metrics, retain quick drill-down affordances, and minimize layout shifts during card collapse/expand transitions across Chrome, Safari (mobile & desktop), and Firefox. This work covers new compact card variants, chart fallbacks, modal anchoring behavior when charts expand, and cross-browser CSS fallbacks for sticky headers and overflow handling.
acceptance_criteria: Compact card variant available for small viewports (<= 480px) with single-line metric + tappable sparkline preview
Tap-and-hold or horizontal swipe gestures reveal secondary metrics without navigating away
Keyboard and screen-reader accessible equivalents for all gestures
Sparklines degrade to pre-rendered SVG or lightweight canvas fallback on older Safari builds to avoid layout jank
Modal launched from a card anchors under the card on small screens and preserves scroll position on close
Performance budget: card open/close animation < 70ms on mid-range mobile devices
Design sign-off from Product and Engineering and a prototype validated with 6 usability sessions
design_decisions: Use a single DOM card with CSS transform-based expansion rather than mounting/unmounting subtrees to reduce reflow
Prefer SVG sparklines for high-DPI clarity, with canvas fallback for >500 datapoints to avoid paint churn
Implement horizontal pan to reveal secondary metrics on touch; provide focusable toggle buttons as keyboard equivalents
Use IntersectionObserver to lazy-render charts offscreen to keep initial paint fast
Adopt a compact typography scale and truncate labels with ellipses and full-value tooltips on hover/focus
tradeoffs: CSS Grid provides simpler multi-column collapsing but required additional polyfills for older Safari — we chose flexbox for predictable cross-browser wrap behavior
Animating height causes layout thrash on some mobile Safari builds; we animate transforms and mask overflow for smoother transitions at the expense of slightly more complex clipping rules
Providing both gesture and keyboard affordances increases DOM complexity but is necessary for accessibility compliance
SVG offers crispness but has higher DOM node cost for many datapoints; we only use SVG for <500 points and canvas for higher-density traces

test_plan: Run 6 moderated mobile usability sessions (iOS Safari and Android Chrome) to validate discoverability of gestures
Cross-browser visual QA for Chrome, Safari (macOS & iOS), Firefox on Windows — focus on overflow clipping, sticky headers, and modal anchoring
Accessibility audit: keyboard navigation, ARIA live regions for metric updates, screen-reader narration of expanded state
Performance tests on mid-range Android (e.g., Pixel 4a) and iPhone SE to ensure open/close < 70ms
E2E smoke tests verifying card drill-down routes and preserving scroll position after modal close
